items.title: Don't warn about overwritten static transforms in the selection panel
items.body:
### Related

* Closes #12853

### What

Selecting a static named-transform component (e.g. the `child_frame` column of a `/tf_static` entity loaded from an MCAP) showed the generic warning _"When a static component is logged multiple times, only the last value is stored. Previously logged values are overwritten and not recoverable."_

That text is false for named transforms (`Transform3D`/`Pinhole` with parent/child frame references): the store never discards them, so nothing was actually lost (see the discussion in #12853). The panel now shows a neutral informational label instead, whose tooltip explains that every logged static transform is preserved.

To make the store's existing knowledge available to the viewer, the private `is_transform_archetype` in `re_chunk_store::writes` is now exposed (and renamed to) `re_chunk_store::preserves_static_transforms`, as suggested in the issue thread.

* `crates/store/re_chunk_store/src/writes.rs` — `pub fn preserves_static_transforms` (renamed from `is_transform_archetype`, unchanged semantics).
* `crates/viewer/re_data_ui/src/latest_all_instance_ui.rs` — look up the component's archetype via the store schema and use the info label for transform archetypes.

### Details

* The store-side behavior is unchanged — only the UI message changes.
* The separate "multiple static transforms are not inspectable in the streams tree/selection panel" limitation from the issue thread is out of scope here (as also suggested in the thread).

### Test plan

- [x] New kittest snapshot `selection_panel_component_static_transform_overwrite` covering a single static chunk with three transform rows (the `/tf_static` MCAP shape): `cargo test -p re_selection_panel --all-features -- selection_panel_component_static`
- [x] Existing `selection_panel_component_static_overwrite` snapshot (Points2D) unchanged — non-transform static data still shows the warning. Verified its reference PNG is untouched.
- [x] Sabotage run: with the UI fix reverted, the new snapshot test fails (warning alert rendered); with the fix it passes.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p re_chunk_store -p re_data_ui -p re_selection_panel --all-features --all-targets` — clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` and `scripts/lint.py` — clean.
- [x] `cargo test -p re_chunk_store -p re_data_ui -p re_selection_panel --all-features` — all pass, including the existing static-transform store tests (`static_transforms_spread_across_chunks_are_preserved`, `static_non_transform_data_spread_across_chunks_is_deduplicated`).

*Note: implemented with the help of an AI coding agent; I have read and understand the full change.*

Labels: probably `🪳 bug` — the false warning shipped in released versions, so it seems changelog-worthy, but happy to switch to `exclude from changelog` if you consider this too minor.

items.title: Fix --detach-process for standalone CLI
items.body:
### Related

* Closes #11847

### What

`--detach-process` was copied into `StartupOptions`, but that field is never read by the standalone CLI, so the viewer kept running in the invoking process.

This change relaunches native-viewer CLI invocations once as a detached child:

* preserves the original CLI arguments and inserts a hidden child marker before any `--` end-of-options separator to prevent recursion;
* starts a new session with `setsid` on Unix and uses `DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows;
* disconnects standard streams so captured pipes do not keep the launcher attached;
* leaves subcommands, headless/server/web/save/test/version modes in the original process.

Focused tests cover the one-time relaunch guard, representative native-viewer invocations, `rerun --detach-process -- recording.rrd`, and the modes that must remain attached.

### Testing

* `cargo test -p rerun --lib --no-default-features --features rerun/native_viewer,rerun/run detach_` (Windows and Linux; 3 passed on each)
* `cargo clippy -p rerun --lib --no-default-features --features rerun/native_viewer,rerun/run -- --deny warnings` (Windows and Linux)
* `cargo fmt -p rerun -- --check` (Windows and Linux)
* `cargo check -p rerun --lib --tests --no-default-features --features rerun/native_viewer,rerun/run` (Linux)
* `cargo build -p rerun-cli --no-default-features --features rerun-cli/native_viewer` (Linux)
* `pixi run lint-codegen`
* Changed-file fast lint checks for Rustfmt, TOML formatting, repository lint, typos, and notebook stripping
* Windows lifecycle test: the launcher exited successfully in 546 ms, the detached child was observed alive, produced a screenshot, and exited without a leftover process
* Linux lifecycle test: the launcher returned in 0 seconds, the child was observed with `PID == SID == PGID`, wrote a 124,236-byte PNG, and terminated

### Confidence

High. The dead data flow was reproduced on current `main`; both platform-specific paths compile, Windows and Linux process lifecycles were validated end to end, and viewer/non-viewer mode selection plus end-of-options handling have regression coverage.

items.title: Add signal heatmap and audio clip views
items.body:
### Related

* Closes #2852

### What

This PR adds first-class support for audio-oriented datasets in three layers:

* New `AudioClip` and `AudioAnnotation` archetypes for PCM tensors, sample-rate metadata, channel names, and timestamp-window text spans, generated across Rust/Python/C++ docs and SDK surfaces.
* A new `AudioView` that renders logged audio clips as time-aligned waveforms, supports per-channel visibility, mixdown display, PCM playback on native and web, looped region playback, WAV export for the full clip or selected loop region, viewer-side Hanning/Hamming and low/high/band-pass processing controls, ASR span overlays, and scrubbing the global Rerun time cursor by clicking/dragging in the waveform.
* A richer signal heatmap example that can load PCM WAV files or decode common compressed formats through `ffmpeg`, logs raw audio, waveform scalars, STFT/mel/MFCC/channel spectrogram tensors, streaming windows, ASR word spans, timestamped text tokens, and NumPy helper variants for Hanning/Hamming windows plus low/high/band-pass filtered spectrograms.

#### Issue coverage

| Original ask | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Play audio as time-series data | Adds `AudioClip` plus `AudioView` waveform display on the timeline. Native and web builds can play logged PCM tensors from the current time cursor or a looped region. The example can load PCM WAV input with `--wav` or decode common compressed audio via `--audio` and `ffmpeg`. |
| Plot changing spectrograms as audio plays / pinpoint timestamp and features / MFCC | Adds `SignalHeatmapView` for precomputed signal tensors, range-concatenates streaming chunks, and the example logs STFT, mel, MFCC, channel STFT, and streaming windows. `AudioView` and heatmap views share the global time cursor. |
| Play individual channels separately or multiple channels combined | `AudioView` supports per-channel visibility, visual mixdown, playback of the enabled channels, playback of a mono mixdown, and WAV export using the same channel/mixdown selection. |
| Correlate timestamp-window with ASR text output | Adds `AudioAnnotation` spans and renders labeled ASR windows directly in `AudioView`; the example also logs timestamped tokens in `TextLogView`. |
| Nice-to-have windows and filters | `AudioView` has viewer-side Hanning/Hamming window controls and low-pass/high-pass/band-pass filter controls that affect display and playback. The example also logs precomputed filter/window heatmap variants. |

#### Review notes

* `SignalHeatmapView` displays precomputed signal tensors instead of computing STFT/MFCC inside the viewer. The example includes NumPy-only helpers so users can produce the expected tensors without taking a dependency on a heavier audio stack.
* `tinyaudio` is used for playback because it provides a small cross-platform callback API and already has native plus WebAudio backends. Linux enables its `alsa` feature explicitly; the existing workspace dependency is reused.
* `AudioView` exports PCM16 WAV bytes directly instead of adding an encoder dependency.
* The example's `--audio` path uses a user's local `ffmpeg` executable only when requested, keeping the default example dependencies unchanged.

#### Screenshot

![Signal heatmap and audio views running in Rerun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reza2kn/rerun-codex-fork/codex/pr-assets/pr-assets/12842/signal_heatmap_viewer_6b8802f.png)

Captured from `.context/pr-screenshots/signal_heatmap.rrd` with the current branch viewer using the native Metal renderer.

items.title: Default Safari to WebGL — Safari 26.4 broke 3D under WebGPU

labels.name: 🕸️ web
labels.description: regarding running the viewer in a browser

items.body:
The viewer previously defaulted Safari to WebGPU on macOS 26 Tahoe+, where WebGPU was newly enabled. Safari 26.4 (released 2026-03-23) has since regressed 3D rendering under WebGPU: the Spatial 3D viewport renders black on macOS 26.4 and iPadOS 26.4, while every other view type renders correctly. iOS 26.3 still works — confirming the regression entered with Safari 26.4 across all WebKit clients.

This restores the Safari → WebGL fallback by re-grouping Safari with Firefox in `default_backends()` and re-adding the `is_safari_browser()` helper to `device_caps.rs`. It is a near-pure revert of rerun-io/rerun@76bd562982 (with updated TODO issue ref).

**Note:** this is a mitigation, not a root-cause fix. The underlying Safari WebGPU bug is tracked in rerun-io/rerun#12788; that issue should remain open until Safari ships a fix and we can re-enable WebGPU as the default on Safari.

### Related

* rerun-io/rerun#12788 — underlying Safari WebGPU 3D rendering bug (kept open intentionally)

### What

Affects only the default graphics backend selection on Safari. No view-type, visualizer, or data-handling code paths change. Safari users will now use WebGL by default; the "Restart with WebGPU" menu option (and the `?renderer=webgpu` URL parameter) remain available for users who want to opt in.

### Testing

Verified via locally built web viewer (`pixi run rerun-web`) on:

| OS / Device | Safari | Result |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 26.4.1 Tahoe (M5) | 26.4 (21624.1.16.11.4) | ✅ defaults to WebGL, 3D renders |
| iPadOS 26.4.2 | 26.4 | ✅ defaults to WebGL, 3D renders |
| iOS 26.3.1 (iPhone 17) | 26.3 | ✅ defaults to WebGL, 3D renders |
| macOS 15.7.4 Sequoia | 18.6 | ✅ defaults to WebGL (already did pre-change) |

Confirmed in each case via the viewer menu showing "Restart with WebGPU" (i.e. WebGL is the active backend). Chrome and Firefox on Tahoe unaffected by this change.

### Compatibility

No compatibility impact. This is a runtime default for graphics backend selection — no changes to data formats, SDK APIs, or persisted state. Users who have explicitly forced WebGPU via the `?renderer=webgpu` URL parameter retain that override.

items.title: Support `BinaryStream` in `set_sinks()` for multi-sink streaming with Gradio

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

items.body:
I HEAVILY used claude code for this, I did test with my gradio implementation to make sure it actually worked, and the changes are minimal so hopefully this is reasonable. 


### Related

<!--
Include links to any related issues/PRs in a bulleted list, for example:
* Closes #1234
* Part of #1337
-->
Closes rerun-io/rerun#11441

### What

<!--
Make sure the PR title and labels are set to maximize their usefulness for the CHANGELOG,
and our `git log`.

If you have noticed any breaking changes, include them in the migration guide.

We track various metrics at <https://build.rerun.io>.

For maintainers:
* To run all checks from `main`, comment on the PR with `@rerun-bot full-check`.
* To deploy documentation changes immediately after merging this PR, add the `deploy docs` label.

For more details check the PR section on <https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
-->

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c03dd8f-146a-4c90-bd31-7294302a3d3a

Allow `BinaryStream` to be used alongside `FileSink` and `GrpcSink` in `set_sinks()`, enabling simultaneous streaming to a web viewer (Gradio in particular) and saving to disk from a single recording.

Previously, `set_sinks()` only accepted `FileSink` and `GrpcSink`, which meant Gradio apps that needed both live binary streaming and file persistence couldn't work. Now users can write:

    stream = recording.binary_stream()
    rr.set_sinks(rr.FileSink("output.rrd"), stream, recording=recording)

    recording.log(...)
    chunk = stream.read()   # for live viewer streaming
    # output.rrd also receives all logged data automatically

Implementation:
- Add `BinaryStreamStorage::create_sink()` to create a new `BinaryStreamSink` sharing the same `Arc<Mutex<...>>` buffer, so data written by the multi-sink can be read from the original storage.
- Implement `MultiSinkCompatible` (sealed trait) for `BinaryStreamSink` so it can participate in `MultiSink`.
- Add `PyBinarySinkStorage` downcast branch in the Python FFI `set_sinks()` to resolve `BinaryStream` objects into Rust sinks.
- Update Python `sinks.py` to include `BinaryStream` in `LogSinkLike` type alias and unwrap it to its inner storage before crossing the FFI boundary.

Minimal gradio example showing how to stream + save at the same time
```python
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Final

import cv2
import gradio as gr
import rerun as rr
import rerun.blueprint as rrb
from gradio_rerun import Rerun
from jaxtyping import UInt8
from numpy import ndarray

RRD_SAVE_DIR: Final[Path] = Path("data") / "rrd-gradio-saves"
RRD_SUFFIX: Final[str] = ".rrd"


def get_recording(recording_id: uuid.UUID | None, application_id: str = "Application ID") -> rr.RecordingStream:
    return rr.RecordingStream(application_id=application_id, recording_id=recording_id)


BLUR_BLUEPRINT = rrb.Blueprint(
    rrb.Horizontal(
        rrb.Spatial2DView(origin="image/original"),
        rrb.Spatial2DView(origin="image/blurred"),
    ),
    collapse_panels=True,
)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SimpleAppState:
    """Session-local recording metadata and buffered stream bytes."""

    recording_id: uuid.UUID
    """Recording identifier reused for incremental logging."""
    rrd_buffer: bytearray = field(default_factory=bytearray)
    """In-memory copy of every chunk streamed to the viewer."""


def log_img_blur_multi_sink(
    state: SimpleAppState, image: UInt8[ndarray, "height width 3"]
) -> Generator[tuple[SimpleAppState, bytes], None, None]:
    recording: rr.RecordingStream = get_recording(recording_id=state.recording_id)

    # Create a binary stream bound to the recording
    stream: rr.BinaryStream = recording.binary_stream()

    # Use set_sinks to ALSO save to a file alongside the binary stream
    RRD_SAVE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    save_path = RRD_SAVE_DIR / f"{state.recording_id}{RRD_SUFFIX}"
    rr.set_sinks(
        rr.FileSink(str(save_path)),
        stream,
        recording=recording,
    )

    recording.send_blueprint(BLUR_BLUEPRINT)
    recording.set_time("iteration", sequence=0)
    recording.log("image/original", rr.Image(image))

    chunk: bytes | None = stream.read()
    if chunk is not None:
        yield state, chunk

    blur: UInt8[ndarray, "height width 3"] = image.copy()
    for i in range(50):
        recording.set_time("iteration", sequence=i)

        time.sleep(0.1)
        blur = cv2.GaussianBlur(blur, (5, 5), 0)
        recording.log("image/blurred", rr.Image(blur))

        chunk = stream.read()
        if chunk is not None:
            yield state, chunk

    chunk = stream.read()
    if chunk is not None:
        yield state, chunk


def verify_and_return_rrd(state: SimpleAppState) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Return the saved .rrd file for download and verify its contents."""
    save_path = RRD_SAVE_DIR / f"{state.recording_id}{RRD_SUFFIX}"
    if not save_path.exists():
        return None, "No saved .rrd file found."

    file_path = str(save_path)

    try:
        recording = rr.recording.load_recording(save_path)
        schema = recording.schema()

        entity_paths = schema.entity_paths()
        archetypes = schema.archetypes()
        index_names = [c.name for c in schema.index_columns()]

        has_original = any("image/original" in p for p in entity_paths)
        has_blurred = any("image/blurred" in p for p in entity_paths)
        has_iteration = "iteration" in index_names

        lines = [
            f"Verified {save_path.name}:",
            f"  Entity paths: {entity_paths}",
            f"  Archetypes: {archetypes}",
            f"  Timelines: {index_names}",
            f"  image/original present: {has_original}",
            f"  image/blurred present: {has_blurred}",
            f"  'iteration' timeline: {has_iteration}",
            f"  File size: {save_path.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB",
        ]

        if not has_original or not has_blurred:
            lines.append("  WARNING: Missing expected entity paths!")
        if not has_iteration:
            lines.append("  WARNING: Missing 'iteration' timeline!")

        return file_path, "\n".join(lines)
    except Exception as e:
        return file_path, f"Verification failed: {e}"


def build() -> gr.Blocks:
    with gr.Blocks() as demo:
```

items.title: When scrubbing time, intelligently round to a nice value
items.body:
### Related
* Part of https://linear.app/rerun/issue/RR-2768/improve-time-selection-experience-on-a-timeline

### What
When dragging the time cursor ("time scrubbing") we would previously pick arbitrarily precise time points, regardless of zoom level. Now, we snap to the "simplest" value that is within a pixel from the mouse cursor. The simplest value is defined as the one with _the most_ trailing zeroes (e.g. prefer `23.500000` over `23.484793`).

### Before
Even though we zoomed out to where we are viewing full hours, when we try to pick a time we select with microsecond precision:

![dumb-aim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22a10523-a7a9-4474-909f-e61e11a8f551)


### After
Notice how we start by picking whole multiples of 10s, but as we zoom in we pick multiples of 0.5s, and then 5ms, 10us, etc.

![smart-aim](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9508f33-b724-43fe-8037-a4f5f33c0480)

Note that we only ever omit _zeroes_ in the display, so this is a real difference in how values are picked, NOT how they are displayed!


### Future work
* Coarser snapping when a modifier key is pressed
* Set the time display precision based on zoom level

items.title: GPU box cloud renderer for Boxes3D (#10276)
items.body:
Implements a new fast rendering path for Boxes3D that uses GPU-accelerated box cloud rendering when handling large numbers of solid boxes without rotations. This provides significant performance improvements for scenes with 1000+ boxes.

Closes #10276.

Implementation:

- New BoxCloudBuilder and box_cloud renderer using procedural GPU geometry
- Stores box data (centers, half-sizes, colors) in textures for GPU access
- Generates box geometry procedurally in vertex shader from unit cube
- Fast path automatically selected for solid boxes above threshold

Data handling:

- Properly clamps half_sizes, centers, and transforms to num_instances
- Applies per-instance transforms from transform tree to component centers
- Generates correct bounding boxes, labels, and picking data for all instances

Eligibility checking:

- Checks all per-instance transforms for rotation/scaling, not just first
- Falls back to slow path when any transform is non-trivial
- Falls back for wireframe modes and per-instance rotation components

Testing and benchmarks:

- Added boxes3d_fast_path regression test with kittest snapshots
- Added Criterion benchmarks measuring actual GPU rendering performance
- Benchmarks integrated into CI reusable_bench workflow
- All existing transform tests continue to pass

Performance results:

- 1,000 boxes: 1.58ms per frame (632K boxes/sec)
- 10,000 boxes: 664us per frame (15M boxes/sec)
- 50,000 boxes: ~1.5ms per frame (33M boxes/sec)

items.title: Viewer now crops incoming chunks if time range was requested
items.body:
### Related

* Fixes https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10692
* This is in many ways just part of a workaround for inspecting large episodes, making it related to https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/11315

### What

Datastore URLs allow querying only a time range. This then leads us to pulling down the necessary chunks, causing arbitrarily more data in the Viewer to arrive, depending on how big the chunks are.

This PR introduces crop-on-insert in order to crop chunks to the specified range, thus honoring the previously requested time bounds more accurately.
@abey79 and me decided to crop only on the specified timeline (not cropping on any other) and allow recombining cropped chunks into an existing store. This video demonstrates what this means in practice and feature some slight ui changes:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/395223c3-4025-439f-a9ae-806f191713f2


While the cropping itself is a saimple range query on incoming chunks, in practice this gives rise to a whole slew of issues like how to deal with overlapping data, chunk ids, row ids, etc.. The most important ones like "what happens if I load the recording after all" & "what happens if I load overlapping ranges" are well-enough addressed here, but it's not a clean solution overall as you easily may end up in a situation with duplicated data in-memory.
I firmly believe that we should remove this mechanism again once we have dynamic occupancy handling for continuous streaming within a memory budget (#11315). We'll still want a way to highlight selected time ranges, but we can do that on a per-visualization basis as needed.

items.body:
Depends on:
* ~~https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/9044~~

Syntax:
```
rerun+http://addr:port/recording/<recording-id>?time_range=<timeline>@<min>s?..<max>s?
```

The `s` suffix means "seconds", and if present, we assume the given `timeline` is temporal. If it is absent, we assume it is a sequence timeline.

Examples:

```sh
# Temporal timeline
rerun+http://127.0.0.1:51234/recording/c2c6bef6-5bdb-43a8-8563-ce878b238936?time_range=stable_time@1.1198s..3.4998s

# Sequence timeline
rerun+http://127.0.0.1:51234/recording/c2c6bef6-5bdb-43a8-8563-ce878b238936?time_range=log_tick@200..500
```

Also added a new UI command, `CopyTimeRangeLink` (only available from command palette for now), which constructs a redap URL from the active recording ID + loop selection. You need to have a redap recording loaded for that to work.

To test:
1. Build `rgbd` (or any other large-ish interesting recording)
   ```
   pixi run -e wheel-test py-build-common
   pixi run -e wheel-test build-examples rrd --channel release --examples rgbd example_data
   ```
1. Start a catalog server on localhost
1. Register the `rgbd` recording
1. `pixi run rerun-web`
1. Once browser tab opens, change `?url=` to (percent-encoded, e.g. using browser dev tools `encodeURIComponent`) `rerun+http://127.0.0.1:51234/recording/<rgbd-recording-id>`
1. Create a loop selection (shift + left mouse button drag on the timeline)
1. <kbd>CMD + P</kbd> -> `Copy link to selected time range`
1. Open a new tab and paste the link in

items.title: Add selection change and time(line) change callbacks to Jupyter Notebook and JS APIs

labels.name: 🕸️ web
labels.description: regarding running the viewer in a browser

items.body:
* Part of https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/9169

## What

This PR adds basic selection and timeline callbacks to the Viewer:
* `selectionchange`: Fired when an item is selected.
  * We only expose `View`, `Container`, `Entity`, and `Instance`.
* `timelinechange`: Fired when the active timeline changes.
* `timeupdate`: Fired when the time on the active timeline changes.

These callbacks are exposed in the Web Viewer:

```ts
// We use the Node `EventEmitter` pattern in JS:
viewer.on("selectionchange", (selection) => console.log(selection));
```

And in Jupyter Notebooks:

```py
from rerun_notebook import Viewer, ViewerCallbacks

# We (Jan and Gijs) chose to expose this as a class that you inherit from:
class MyCallbacks(ViewerCallbacks):
  def on_selection_change(self, selection):
    print(selection)

# Which is then passed to a `Viewer` instance:
viewer = Viewer()
viewer.register_callbacks(MyCallbacks())
```

Because of how these callbacks pass through the Web Viewer, they are technically also exposed in Rust, via `StartupOptions`. I'm not sure how far we want to take that, so I didn't expose it all the way through the top-level `rerun` crate.

items.title: Provide APIs to log arbitrary data to recording properties

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

items.body:
### Related

* Closes: #9199 

### What

This PR should cover all use-cases that we could come up with so far and be flexible enough to extend into the future without breaking changes. Here is the gist:
* We map a property name to an `EntityPath` that lives at `/__partition_properties/<property-name>`. Builtin recording properties (name, start time) will be at the special path `/__partition_properties/recording`.
  * Nothing lives directly at the root.
  * The current `RecordingProperties` archetype stays as is.
* The value of a property is always an archetype (potentially AnyValues). In the future we might open this up to specify general Arrow values.
* The API will be: `rec.send_property(name: str, archetype: AsComponent | [AsComponent])`
  * Motivation: `send_` signals that the properties are not guaranteed in a distributed setting.
  * `name` is positional, so we can upgrade it to reflect hierarchies later without breaking user code. (For example by renaming to `entity_path`).
* For now we don't expose the fact that this modeling allows for hierarchical grouping of properties.
* We will have to special methods to set the builtin properties:
  * `send_recording_name`

items.title: Fix WSL support, update troubleshooting guide
items.body:
## Related

* Fixes https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8564
* Some steps towards https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8475
* Dependent on https://github.com/emilk/egui/pull/5506
* Dependent on https://github.com/emilk/egui_plot/pull/67

## What

### What's broken

Since Rerun 0.19 we picking in 2D & 3D view was broken & accompanied by log spam.

The reason we failed 0.19+ is unknown but likely either that something caused us picking the "webgl-like" compatibility tier or a change in wgpu no longer allows us to texture copy depth buffers.

Rerun 0.21 then broke startup entirely. This happens due to two distinct problems
* we added a check that foresees the picking issue, aborts application start and tells the user to update their driver (which.. as far as I tried doesn't help)
* wgpu did a validation related thing that that accidentally makes us fail startup because it makes the assumption that compute shader support == glsl support for buffers with runtime size (very very reasonable, but also wrong it turns out :sob: https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/6841)

### This Fix

I decided to move forward more aggressively in a manner that leaves all these intertwined issues behind and sets us up better for simpler & more advanced rendering in the future:
* the troubleshooting guide now explains how to update the mesa drivers
* we configure wgpu now such that it allows picking those non-compliant Vulkan drivers

-> As a result we can draw with Vulkan rather than a (typically) outdated GL driver which is in line with us moving slowly towards WebGPU support as the minspec.
(See code comments for remaining weirdness ;-))

Turns out another benefit with this is that multi-gpu setups behave like on the host now: Previously, `MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME` had to be set to pick which adapter is used. Now all adapters are passed through WSL correctly, meaning that our regular adapter selection logic (which is to be further improved) works fine, i.e. it prefers discrete over integrated GPU unless `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low` is set.

* Ubuntu 22.04
* Ubuntu 24.04

previous tests indicate that Ubuntu 20 should behave similar to 22.

Tracking issue: #7897 

This implements basic graph primitives in the Rerun data model. This is a first step towards visualizing node-link diagrams in Rerun (related issue: #6898).

In addition to the changes to the data model, this PR adds two example crates, `node_link_graph` and `graph_view` to the Rust examples that show how these primitives can be used.

## Design Decisions

- Nodes and edges are stored as `components` and can be batched. To have a single node per entity we can use Rerun’s [[clamping mechanism](https://rerun.io/docs/concepts/batches#component-clamping)](https://rerun.io/docs/concepts/batches#component-clamping).
- `GraphNodeId` is modeled as ~`u32` to improve performance when using `petgraph`~ strings for better user experience.
- A node is unique identified by combining its `GraphNodeId` and its `EntityPath`.
- Labels of the nodes can be set via the `labels` component and toggled via `show_labels`
- ~Hierarchical graphs can be modeled through entity paths. For edges that cross entity boundaries we can insert dummy nodes to properly render subparts of the hierarchy.~
- ~Nodes and edges need to be logged to the same entity, otherwise the selections will collide. We provider helper functions / conversions to link nodes that are stored in different entities.~

> [!WARNING]
> This PR has changed considerably from its initial version:
> * No linking of nodes between entities (an therefore hierarchy) yet.
> * For now, Graphs are local only and therefore have to be logged to the same entity.

## Logging example

```rs
rec.log(
        "simple",
        &rerun::GraphNodes::new(["a", "b", "c"])
            .with_positions([(0.0, 100.0), (-100.0, 0.0), (100.0, 0.0)])
            .with_labels(["A", "B", "C"]),
    )?;
    // Note: We log to the same entity here.
    rec.log(
        "simple",
        &rerun::GraphEdges::new([("a", "b"), ("b", "c"), ("c", "a")]).with_directed_edges(),
    )?;
```

items.body:
### What

Map Space View for GNSS/GPS data logged through new GPS Coordinates archetype.    

https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/assets/82426/86b13ba3-97af-47d2-9422-7052d7064265


- Added a new `re_space_view_map` crate for visualizing `Points3D` with gps coordinates. 
  - `map_visualizer_system.rs` implements the `VisualizerSystem` trait. It has only one meaningful function, that takes the `Positions3D` components and turns into `vec<MapEntry>` array along with optional `Color` and `Radius` components. This `vec<MapEntry>` is the only field of the `MapVisualizerSystem`. 
  - `map_space_view.rs` is where the magic happens. It uses `walkers` slippy map implementation to show an OpenStreetMap or Mapbox map. On the `selection_ui ` you can change the map providers. To view Mapbox maps, you need to set mapbox tokens (you can get free tokens from Mapbox's site) and pass it via the env variable (`MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`) or via the blueprint
  - `map_windows.rs` is a small helper to show the zoom controls and acknowledgment on the UIs. 
- For blueprints I made `MapProvider` component (enum with providers+styles), and a `MapOptions` archetype. 

The logging of data is performed as follows:

```rust
//! Log some GPS coordinates

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let rec = rerun::RecordingStreamBuilder::new("rerun_example_gps_coordinates").spawn()?;

    rec.log(
        "points",
        &rerun::Points3D::new([(47.6344, 19.1397, 0.0), (47.6344, 19.1399, 1.0)]),
    )?;

    Ok(())
}
```

The blueprint is defined as follows:

```python
"""Use a blueprint to show a map."""

import rerun as rr
import rerun.blueprint as rrb

rr.init("rerun_example_gps_coordinates", spawn=True)

rr.log("points", Points3D([[47.6344, 19.1397, 0], [47.6334, 19.1399, 1]]))

# Create a map view to display the chart.
blueprint = rrb.Blueprint(
    rrb.MapView(
        origin="points",
        name="MapView",
        map_options=rrb.archetypes.MapOptions(provider=rrb.components.MapProvider.MapboxStreets),
    ),
    collapse_panels=True,
)

rr.send_blueprint(blueprint)
```

The PR is not perfect, but the view is usable.  

Please review the changes and evaluate their potential utility for your needs. If you don't like, prefer not to merge just close it - no hard feelings. 

### To be discussed

 * Check with you guys to see if the name is right at all. Maybe instead of GPS we can go with something better
 * Position3D is limited to `f32` instead of `f64`. This makes it less precise than `/NavSatFix`

items.body:
### What

Previously, the dataframe view would switch between "latest at" and "time range" mode implicitly, based on any single one view entity having its visible time range overridden. This has several problem:

items.title: Simplify blueprint API by removing Viewport concept

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

labels.name: exclude from changelog
labels.description: PRs with this won't show up in CHANGELOG.md

items.body:
### What
In writing the documentation I realized the distinction between the `rrb.Blueprint` object and the `rrb.Viewport` object was not meaningful enough to warrant its own concept for the user.

Practically, the only time a user would ever use `rrb.Viewport` was to set `auto_layout`, `auto_space_views`, (and maybe maximized if we expose an API for that). Most of the other time they use a `ContainerLike` anyways. This makes introducing the extra `Viewport` indirection just feel like cognitive overhead.

This moves the viewport properties to `rrb.Blueprint` object directly, and makes the viewport just be a single optional `ContainerLike` on the blueprint.

Before:
```
ContainerLike: Container | SpaceView

Viewport:
  root_container: ContainerLike
  auto_layout: bool
  auto_space_views: bool

ViewportLike: Viewport | ContainerLIke


Blueprint:
  viewport: ViewportLike
  blueprint_panel: BlueprintPanel
  selection_panel: SelectionPanel
  time_panel: TimePanel
```

After
```
ContainerLike: Container | SpaceView

Blueprint:
  viewport: ContainerLike
  blueprint_panel: BlueprintPanel
  selection_panel: SelectionPanel
  time_panel: TimePanel
  auto_layout: bool
  auto_space_views: bool
```
